mainTopic: Full years in the ברייתא, the ruling of רבי יוסי בן כיפר, and the order of the signs of maturity in the new פרק
overview: This amud first finishes a ברייתא that lists 'years' counted as full years from the exact date, not as calendar years. The examples are a sold field, the six years of an עבד עברי, and the years of a son and a daughter. רב says the years of a son and daughter refer to ערכין. רב יוסף says they refer to the ages in our פרק, יוצא דופן. The two do not truly argue: each one is reading the ברייתא's wording differently. Next, רבי אלעזר rules like רבי יוסי בן כיפר, and when רבי זירא asks him in person, he explains that his ruling comes from reasoning about the משנה's wording. The פרק then ends with a הדרן. A new פרק opens with a משנה about the two signs of a girl's maturity. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about the case where the upper sign appears before the lower one. The גמרא explains why the משנה says 'even though it is impossible.' It then defends the חכמים against two פסוקים in יחזקאל, and the explanation of the second פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three harvests in two years: the field is counted in full years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes reading the פסוק about a sold field. 'Years of crops' shows that the buyer may sometimes collect three harvests in two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Years of crops he shall sell to you': sometimes you sell three crops in two years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof that the two years of a sold שדה אחוזה are full years. Because of this, the buyer can end up with three harvests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of years and of crops, but it does not tie the number of years to the number of crops. If the years were calendar years, the count would line up with the harvests. Because they are full years from the date of sale, a buyer who bought before a harvest can collect three crops before two full years pass.

keyTerms.meaning: Crops, harvests
An inherited family field that can be sold and later redeemed
Sometimes

phrases.english: 'years of crops he shall sell to you'
phrases.notes: This is the end of a פסוק quoted just before this point: ויקרא 25:15.

phrases.english: sometimes you sell
three crops in two years.
phrases.notes: For example, he buys the field just before a harvest and collects two more harvests before two full years are up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source for the field case, which began just before this point
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording 'years of crops' shows that full years are counted, so three harvests can fall within two years

steps.title: Where do we learn that a Hebrew slave's six years are full years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in the ברייתא and asks for its source: the six years of an עבד עברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The six years of a Hebrew slave: from where do we know them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next case. It asks how we know the six years of an עבד עברי are counted as full years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the six years of an עבד עברי are full years. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק that proves this, just as it did for the field.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish servant, sold for six years
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The six years of a Hebrew slave, from where do we know them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the same ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that an עבד עברי's six years are full years

steps.title: 'And in the seventh': he may also work in the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'and' in 'and in the seventh' teaches that the slave may have to keep working into the seventh calendar year until six full years are done.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Six years he shall work, and in the seventh.' This means he also works in the seventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק. The word 'and' before 'in the seventh' shows that the עבד עברי may still be working during the seventh calendar year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the years were calendar years, he would go free when the seventh calendar year begins. The 'and' tells us he can still be working in the seventh calendar year. That only makes sense if we count six full years from the day he was sold.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק, the verse
And in the seventh (year)
Also

steps.whatToRemember: An עבד עברי serves six full years from the day of sale, even if this runs into a seventh calendar year.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'Six years he shall work, and in the seventh',
phrases.notes: שמות 21:2

phrases.english: meaning: in the seventh too he shall work.
phrases.notes: The proof comes from the little word 'and' attached to 'in the seventh.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'and' in 'and in the seventh' shows he may work into the seventh calendar year, so the six years are full years

steps.title: What law is meant by the years of a son and a daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא also listed the years 'of a son and of a daughter.' The גמרא asks which practical law this refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The years of a son and of a daughter: for what law were they mentioned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last item in the ברייתא and asks what practical law it means. This sets up two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is not 'from where do we know it' but 'where does it apply.' Age matters in many laws, so the גמרא wants to know which case the ברייתא had in mind when it said a child's years are full years.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What is the practical point?
A son and a daughter

phrases.english: Those of a son and of a daughter,
phrases.notes: He means the years of a child's age, which the ברייתא listed as full years.

phrases.english: for what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the last item in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical law the 'years of a son and a daughter' refers to

steps.title: First answer: the law of valuations
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל, quoting רב, says it refers to ערכין. A person's valuation depends on age, and that age is counted in full years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: it is for the law of valuations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the full-year rule for a child's age applies to ערכין. That is the fixed amount a person pledges based on someone's age and gender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of a valuation in the תורה changes at certain ages. So we must know exactly when a person reaches each age, and רב says this is counted from the birth date, in full years.

keyTerms.meaning: Valuations: fixed amounts pledged to the בית המקדש based on a person's age and gender
With regard to

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
for the matter of valuations,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It applies to ערכין: ages are counted in full years from birth

steps.title: Second answer: the age rules in our chapter
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says it refers to the ages mentioned in our פרק, 'יוצא דופן.' Those are full years too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: it is for our chapter, 'יוצא דופן.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different application. Whenever our פרק mentions ages, it means full years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פרק has many age-based laws, such as when a child's vows count or when a girl is considered grown. רב יוסף says the ברייתא is telling us those ages are full years, even where the משנה does not say so.

keyTerms.meaning: Our chapter
A baby born by caesarean section; also the name of the fifth פרק of נדה

steps.confusionAlert: 'יוצא דופן' here is the name of the chapter, taken from its opening words. It does not mean the גמרא is now talking about caesarean births.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
for our chapter of 'Yotze Dofen.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It applies to the ages mentioned in פרק יוצא דופן

steps.title: אביי asks: do you really argue?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether he truly disagrees with רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do you disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רב יוסף whether the two answers are really an argument. This sets up רב יוסף's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different answers to one question might mean that each one rejects the other. אביי wants to know whether רב יוסף holds that the full-year rule does NOT apply to ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: You disagree

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Do you disagree?
phrases.notes: He means: do you disagree with רב, who said ערכין?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether steps 5 and 6 are in conflict
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב יוסף rejects רב's application to ערכין

steps.title: No argument: each said a different true application
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that they do not argue. Each named one place where the rule applies, and both are correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. He said one thing and I said one thing, and we do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that the two answers do not conflict. The full-year rule applies both to ערכין and to the ages in our פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sages can give different answers without arguing, because each is pointing to a different true example. So both applications stand, and the rule of full years for a child's age covers both areas.

keyTerms.meaning: One (thing)
And we do not disagree

steps.whatToRemember: The years of a son and a daughter are full years, both for ערכין and for the age rules in פרק יוצא דופן. רב and רב יוסף do not argue.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a common pattern in the גמרא: two different answers are not always a real argument. Sometimes they simply add to each other.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
he said one thing,
and I said one thing,
and we do not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לָא הוּא אָמַר חֲדָא וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two answers add to each other: both ערכין and the ages in our פרק are counted in full years

steps.title: Proof that רב and רב יוסף do not argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רב יוסף's claim of no argument. רב himself said that every age in our whole פרק is counted in full years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this makes sense too. If you thought they argue, then רב, who said 'for ערכין,' would not hold of full years for יוצא דופן. But רב himself said that the הלכה in our whole פרק is counted in full years (מעת לעת)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for what רב יוסף just said: he and רב are not really arguing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב disagreed with רב יוסף, he would have to say full years do not apply to the ages in יוצא דופן. But we know from another statement of רב that he applies full-year counting to this entire פרק. So רב agrees with רב יוסף's case too, and there is no real argument.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes logical sense
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
They disagree
From a time to the same time; a full, exact period counted from the moment of birth
Name of our פרק (literally 'one born through the side')

phrases.english: And so too it stands to reason,
for if it would enter your mind that they disagree,
the one who said 'for valuations'
phrases.notes: This is רב, from step 5.

phrases.english: does not say it applies to 'Yotze Dofen'
But didn't Rav say:
The halacha in our entire chapter
is counted from time to time!
phrases.notes: He means full years, counted from the exact time of birth to the same time years later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's claim in step 8 that the two do not argue.
steps.raayaObject: That רב and רב יוסף do not disagree
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's own statement that the הלכה throughout this פרק is counted מעת לעת

steps.title: Why did רב mention only ערכין?
steps.stepSummary: If רב agrees about יוצא דופן, why did he pick ערכין as his explanation of the ברייתא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, according to רב, who said 'for ערכין,' why didn't he say 'for יוצא דופן'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know רב agrees, the גמרא asks why he chose ערכין as his example and not יוצא דופן. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both cases are correct, there must be a reason רב named ערכין specifically. The גמרא wants to know what pushed him to that choice.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
But rather; then (moving to a new question)

phrases.english: But, according to the one who said 'for valuations,'

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר לְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say 'for Yotze Dofen'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לַעֲרָכִין, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the proof in step 9: if רב agrees about יוצא דופן, why did he choose ערכין?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב read the ברייתא as referring to ערכין rather than יוצא דופן

steps.title: רב matches the list: years written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The other items in the ברייתא are years written in the תורה. So the 'years of a son and daughter' should also be years written in the תורה, and that means ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like those other items. Just as those are written in the תורה, so too these must be ones that are written in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב read the ברייתא based on the other items listed with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other years in the ברייתא's list are written in the תורה. The ages for ערכין are written in the תורה, but the ages in יוצא דופן are not. So to fit the pattern of the list, רב explained 'son and daughter' as ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to; like
Those (the other items in the list)
That are written (in the Torah)

phrases.english: It is similar to those:
phrases.notes: 'Those' are the other years listed in the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: just as those are written,
so too these are ones that are written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא lists years written in the תורה, so 'son and daughter' must also be years written in the תורה, which means ערכין.

steps.title: רב יוסף's reason: the wording 'son and daughter'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף did not explain the ברייתא as ערכין. If it meant ערכין, it would have used the Torah's words for ערכין, 'male and female.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רב יוסף? He holds that if the ברייתא meant ערכין, then instead of 'of a son and of a daughter' it should have said 'of the male and of the female'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב יוסף did not accept רב's reasoning and picked יוצא דופן instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ערכין the תורה says 'male' and 'female.' The ברייתא says 'son' and 'daughter,' which fits the language of our פרק better. So רב יוסף lets the exact wording decide, while רב lets the pattern of the list decide.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here, רב יוסף)
It should have said; it needed to say
Male and female (the Torah's words in the section on ערכין)

phrases.english: And the other one?
This phrase 'of a son and of a daughter,'
it should have said 'of the male and of the female'!
phrases.notes: Those are the words the Torah uses for ערכין, in ויקרא 27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב יוסף's side, explaining why רב's reasoning in step 11 did not convince him.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's wording 'son and daughter' does not match the תורה's ערכין language 'male and female,' so it must mean יוצא דופן.
steps.whatToRemember: Both agree that full years apply to ערכין and to יוצא דופן. They only differ on which case the ברייתא meant. רב goes by the pattern of the list (years written in the תורה), and רב יוסף goes by the wording ('son and daughter,' not 'male and female').

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר, who reported his view in the name of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of רבי אלעזר: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר, who said his view in the name of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a final ruling on the opinion of רבי יוסי בן כיפר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בן כיפר reported a ruling from רבי אליעזר about the age at which someone with no signs of maturity is judged a סריס. רבי אלעזר now fixes this view as the practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows...
In the name of
A male who never developed the signs of maturity

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar,
phrases.notes: This points back to his ruling, quoted earlier, about the age at which someone with no signs of maturity counts as a סריס.

phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new point: a final הלכה ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר, quoting רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns one opinion among several into the practical law for judging when someone is a סריס.

steps.title: רבי זירא wishes to learn the ruling from רבי אלעזר himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא prays that he will get to go up to ארץ ישראל and hear this ruling straight from רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: May I merit to go up and learn this teaching from the mouth of its master.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא reacts to the ruling. He hopes to hear it in person from the one who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא heard the ruling only secondhand, through רב יצחק בר נחמני. He wanted to go up to ארץ ישראל and receive it directly from רבי אלעזר. This shows how much he valued hearing a teaching from its original source.

keyTerms.meaning: May I merit
A teaching; a ruling
Its master (the one who first said it)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
May I merit and go up
phrases.notes: 'Go up' means going up to ארץ ישראל, where רבי אלעזר lived.

phrases.english: and learn this teaching
from the mouth of its master.
phrases.notes: 'Its master' is רבי אלעזר, who gave the ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A personal reaction to the ruling given in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא wishes to hear רבי אלעזר's ruling in person.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks רבי אלעזר if he really gave this ruling
steps.stepSummary: When רבי זירא gets to ארץ ישראל, he asks רבי אלעזר directly whether he ruled like רבי יוסי בן כיפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he went up, he found רבי אלעזר and asked him: Did you say the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא's prayer from the last step comes true. He meets רבי אלעזר and asks him to confirm the ruling. This question sets up רבי אלעזר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now רבי זירא had only heard the ruling secondhand. Now he asks the source himself. The question opens the door for רבי אלעזר to explain what kind of ruling it was.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, meaning he moved to ארץ ישראל
He found him

phrases.english: When he went up,
phrases.notes: This is רבי זירא going up to ארץ ישראל, just as he prayed for in the last step.

phrases.english: he found Rabbi Elazar.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר?
phrases.english: Did you say the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fulfills רבי זירא's prayer from step 14 and asks about the ruling in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר really ruled like רבי יוסי בן כיפר.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains that his ruling comes from reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says he only said it 'stands to reason.' Every משנה in the chapter says 'one day,' but the last one leaves it out. That supports רבי יוסי בן כיפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: I said it stands to reason. The whole chapter says 'one day,' but here it does not. So we learn that it stands to reason to follow him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that his ruling was based on logic. He did not receive it as a tradition. His proof is the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other משנה in the chapter adds the words 'one day' to its age limits. The last משנה does not. רבי אלעזר says this change must mean something, and it fits רבי יוסי בן כיפר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; a conclusion based on logic
Our chapter
'One day': the extra wording used in the age limits of the chapter's משניות
Learn from this; we can conclude

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's ruling comes from reasoning. It is based on the משנה leaving out 'one day' in its last case.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I said that it stands to reason,
since throughout our whole chapter it teaches 'one day,'
and here it does not teach it,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the last משנה of the chapter.

phrases.english: learn from this
that it stands to reason to follow him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, but as a logical conclusion. It is based on the last משנה not saying 'one day'.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of יוצא דופן
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the chapter יוצא דופן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, יוצא דופן.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter called יוצא דופן. A new chapter starts right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is the traditional goodbye to a finished chapter. It does not add any law. It only marks where the topic changes.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing words said at the end of a chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, Yotzei Dofen.
phrases.notes: יוצא דופן is the name of the chapter that just ended, taken from its first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter יוצא דופן is finished.

steps.title: Lower sign before upper sign: she is an adult for יבום
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה rules that if the lower sign of maturity appears before the upper sign, she may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the lower sign came before the upper sign, she either does חליצה or does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about the signs of a girl's maturity. If the lower sign shows up first, she counts as an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only an adult woman can do חליצה or יבום. So the משנה uses this case to tell us when she is treated as grown up. When the lower sign comes first, there is no doubt, and both options are open to her.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower sign of maturity (two hairs)
The upper sign of maturity (breast development)
Does חליצה, the ceremony that frees her from her late husband's brother
Marries her late husband's brother (יבום)

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the lower sign came
before the upper one came,
she either does chalitza or does yibum.
phrases.notes: The case is a woman whose husband died with no children, so his brother comes into the picture.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא סִימָן הַתַּחְתּוֹן עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּא הָעֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the lower sign comes first, she is an adult and may do חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: Upper sign before lower sign: רבי מאיר says neither
steps.stepSummary: If the upper sign appears before the lower sign, even though that seems impossible, רבי מאיר rules she does neither חליצה nor יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the upper sign came before the lower, even though that is impossible, רבי מאיר says: she does not do חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite order: the upper sign comes first. רבי מאיר says she cannot do חליצה or יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this order is supposed to be 'impossible.' Even so, רבי מאיר will not treat her as a sure adult. To him, it is possible the lower sign never came at all, so she may still be a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though it is impossible; this order of signs is not supposed to happen

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'even though it is impossible' do not mean רבי מאיר agrees that it can't happen. They are the voice of the חכמים, whose view comes right after this. רבי מאיר holds that it can happen, so he does not treat her as a sure adult.

phrases.english: If the upper one came
before the lower one came,
even though it is impossible,
Rabbi Meir says:
she does not do chalitza and does not do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse case of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, if the upper sign comes first, she does neither חליצה nor יבום.

steps.title: The Sages: the upper sign never comes first
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר. They rule she may do חליצה or יבום, because the upper sign cannot appear before the lower sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: she either does חליצה or goes into יבום. This is because the lower sign can come before the upper sign, but the upper sign cannot come before the lower sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its case with the view of the חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treated a woman with only the upper sign as possibly still a minor. The חכמים say the order only works one way: if the upper sign is there, the lower sign must already be there too. So she counts as an adult and may do חליצה or יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: She does חליצה, the ceremony that releases her from the brother-in-law
She marries her late husband's brother (יבום)
The lower sign of maturity
The upper sign of maturity

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים say the order goes only one way: lower can come first, upper cannot. So upper sign present means she is an adult.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
she either does חליצה or goes into יבום,
because they said:
it is possible for the lower sign to come
phrases.notes: The lower sign is the two pubic hairs. The upper sign is the development of the chest.

phrases.english: before the upper sign has come,
but it is impossible for the upper sign to come
before the lower sign has come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ חוֹלֶצֶת אוֹ מִתְיַבֶּמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's opposing view to רבי מאיר's ruling in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the upper sign is present she may do חליצה or יבום, because the upper sign never comes before the lower one.

steps.title: How can the משנה say it came and also say it is impossible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'even though it is impossible' and points out that the משנה also says the upper sign 'came.' That looks like a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה says 'even though it is impossible.' But it also says the upper sign came!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and points out a contradiction inside the משנה's own wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a case where the upper sign came first. In the same breath it calls this impossible. If it really happened, how can it be impossible? And if it is impossible, how can the משנה describe it happening?

keyTerms.meaning: Even though it is impossible
But surely / but look

phrases.english: גמרא:
"Even though it is impossible."
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה in step 19, about the upper sign coming first.

phrases.english: But it did come!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר. וַהֲלֹא בָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the upper sign 'came' and also calls it 'impossible.' Both cannot be true at once.

steps.title: Each phrase follows a different opinion
steps.stepSummary: The word 'came' follows רבי מאיר. The phrase 'even though it is impossible' follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It came' is according to רבי מאיר. 'Even though it is impossible' is according to the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction: the two phrases come from two different sides of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the upper sign really can come first, so the משנה describes the case as 'it came.' The רבנן hold it cannot happen, so the משנה adds 'even though it is impossible' to give their view. There is no contradiction, because each phrase belongs to a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the same as the חכמים in the משנה)

phrases.english: "It came" is according to רבי מאיר,
"even though it is impossible" is according to the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בָּא״ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר״ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the wording between two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה contradicts itself by saying the upper sign came and also that it is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Came' reflects רבי מאיר's view, and 'impossible' reflects the רבנן's view.

steps.title: Why say 'impossible' at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the words 'even though it is impossible.' It could just give both rulings, and we would already understand that the רבנן mean it is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה just teach: 'If the upper sign came, רבי מאיר says she does neither חליצה nor יבום, and the Sages say she does either חליצה or יבום.' I would already know the Sages' reason is that it is impossible!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the משנה for adding words it seems not to need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's ruling already shows they think the upper sign cannot come alone, and their reason is spelled out at the end. So the extra phrase 'even though it is impossible' looks like it adds nothing. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the משנה (just) teach
And I would know (on my own)

phrases.english: But let it teach: "If the upper sign came —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: לֹא חוֹלֶצֶת וְלֹא מִתְיַבֶּמֶת,
phrases.english: רבי מאיר says: she does neither חליצה nor יבום,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ חוֹלֶצֶת אוֹ מִתְיַבֶּמֶת״,
phrases.english: and the Sages say: she either does חליצה or goes into יבום,"
and I would know
that it is because it is impossible!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 22 and asks why the רבנן's phrase is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra words 'even though it is impossible' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן's ruling and stated reason already show they think it is impossible, so the phrase seems extra.

steps.title: Without those words we would think it is about a minority
steps.stepSummary: Without the phrase, we might think the upper sign comes first in a minority of women. Then the argument would just be the usual one about worrying about a minority. The phrase teaches that the רבנן say it never happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה had not said 'even though it is impossible,' I would think that in most women the lower sign comes first and in a few the upper sign comes first. Then רבי מאיר would follow his usual view that we worry about the minority, and the Sages would follow their usual view that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the extra words are needed: they block a wrong reading of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the phrase, we could read the מחלוקת as the well-known argument about whether we worry about a מיעוט. The words 'even though it is impossible' show that the רבנן are not just ignoring a small group. In their view the upper sign never comes first at all.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
First
Following his usual reasoning
He worries about the minority

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן are only saying 'most women' here. The whole point is that, for them, the upper sign never comes first at all. It is not a question of majority and minority.
steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'even though it is impossible' teaches that this argument is not the usual מיעוטא argument. The רבנן hold the upper sign simply cannot come first.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא תְּנָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר״,
phrases.english: If it had not taught "even though it is impossible,"
I would have said:
in most women the lower sign comes first,
and in a minority the upper sign comes first;
and רבי מאיר follows his reasoning
that he worries about the minority,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר is known elsewhere for taking a small minority into account.

phrases.english: and the Sages follow their reasoning
that they do not worry about the minority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא תְּנָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by showing what the extra words teach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the extra words prevent a mistaken reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The upper sign comes first in a minority of women, and the argument is about whether we worry about a minority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words teach that the רבנן hold the upper sign never comes first, so this is not a majority/minority argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a phrase that looks extra in a משנה can be there to rule out a wrong reading of the argument.

steps.title: Even when she was checked, the hairs surely came and fell out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds to the 'we might have thought' of step 24. We might think the dispute is only about a girl who was never checked. If she was checked and no hairs were found, maybe the רבנן would agree with רבי מאיר. The words 'it is impossible' teach that even then, the hairs surely grew and simply fell out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that would only be when she was not checked. But where we checked and did not find hairs, you might say the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר that the upper sign came first. So the משנה teaches us that it is impossible. The hairs certainly came, and they just fell out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 24. It shows how far the words 'it is impossible' reach: they cover even a girl who was checked and had no hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the upper sign could come first in a minority of women, then a girl checked with no hairs would prove she is part of that minority, and the רבנן would have to agree with רבי מאיר. By saying 'impossible,' the משנה shuts that door. For the רבנן, missing hairs after breasts appear only means the hairs grew and fell out.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies (only) to...
An unclear case, here a girl who was never checked
We checked and did not find
The upper sign of maturity: the breasts
So it teaches us
Fell out (said of hairs)

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, the upper sign can never come before the lower sign. If breasts are there and hairs are not, we say the hairs came and fell out.
steps.confusionAlert: The first half of this step ('but where we checked... the רבנן agree') is NOT the conclusion. It is the mistaken 'we might have thought' that the words 'it is impossible' come to reject.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, for the רבנן, she may do חליצה or יבום even if a check finds no hairs.

phrases.english: And that would only apply to an unchecked case,
phrases.notes: This is still the mistaken 'we might have thought' from step 24: the argument about worrying for a minority.

phrases.english: but where we checked her and did not find hairs —

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר מוֹדוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: you might say the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Meir
that the upper sign came first.
So the Mishna teaches us that it is impossible.
The lower sign certainly came,
and it simply fell out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּסְתָמָא, אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּבַדְקַן וְלָא אַשְׁכְּחַן

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה needs the words: they rule out a case we might have thought the רבנן agree with
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן only rely on the majority when she was not checked. If she was checked and had no hairs, they would agree the upper sign came first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן hold it is impossible. Even if no hairs are found, the hairs surely grew and fell out.

steps.title: A פסוק lists breasts before hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן from יחזקאל 16:7, which says 'your breasts were formed and your hair grew.' That order fits רבי מאיר. For the רבנן, the פסוק should have mentioned hair first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי מאיר: that is what the פסוק says, 'Your breasts were formed and your hair grew.' But for the רבנן, it should have said it the other way around!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems to say breasts come before hair, which challenges the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the upper sign (breasts) first and the lower sign (hair) second. If the order of the פסוק shows the order of growing up, it backs רבי מאיר. The רבנן say the hair always comes first, so the פסוק seems backwards for them.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one view), but...
It should have said the reverse
Breasts, the upper sign
Hair, the lower sign

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Meir,
that is what is written:
"Your breasts were formed and your hair grew"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:7

phrases.english: but according to the Rabbis,
it should have said the reverse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to the רבנן, this time from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that the upper sign cannot come before the lower sign
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists breasts before hair, which suggests that is the order of growing up, as רבי מאיר says.

steps.title: Once the breasts appear, we know the hair already grew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not giving the order they grow in. It means: once the breasts are formed, it is known that the hair has already grown.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: since the breasts are formed, it is known that your hair has grown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the פסוק in a new way, so it fits the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order in the פסוק is not the order of growing. It is the order of how we know things: seeing breasts tells us the hair is already there. This actually fits the רבנן well, since for them breasts always mean hair came first.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
Since, once
It is known, it is certain

phrases.english: This is what the verse is saying:
since "the breasts were formed" —
it is known that "your hair has grown."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק lists the signs in the order they grow, breasts first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means that seeing the breasts proves the hair already grew. This fits the רבנן.

steps.title: A second פסוק seems to put breasts first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another פסוק, יחזקאל 23:21, which speaks of Egypt pressing her breasts 'for the sake of' her coming of age. That fits רבי מאיר. For the רבנן, it should have been the reverse. The next step answers this.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי מאיר: that is what the פסוק says, 'When Egypt pressed your nipples, for the sake of your young womanhood.' But for the רבנן, it should have said it the other way around!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge to the רבנן from a different פסוק, in the same style as before. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק describes the breasts already there while the signs of young womanhood (read as the lower sign, hair) are still in the future. That suggests the upper sign can come first, as רבי מאיר says. For the רבנן the order should be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Your nipples / breasts
Signs of your youth; here read as the lower sign of becoming a נערה
Youth, the stage of becoming a young woman

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Meir,
that is what is written:
"When those from Egypt pressed your nipples
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 23:21

phrases.english: for the sake of your young womanhood"
phrases.notes: In this challenge, שְׁדֵי נְעוּרָיִךְ is read as the lower sign, the hairs, which come later in the פסוק.

it should have said the reverse!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב ״בַּעְשׂוֹת מִמִּצְרַיִם דַּדַּיִךְ לְמַעַן שְׁדֵי נְעוּרָיִךְ״

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes breasts already present while the signs of young womanhood are still to come, so the upper sign seems to come first.

steps.title: The verse means: once the breasts came, the hair surely came
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from יחזקאל 23:21 the same way it answered the first פסוק. The פסוק does not give the order of growth. It tells us that once the breasts have come, it is known that the hair already came.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: once your breasts have come, it is known that your signs of youth (the hair) have come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 28. It explains the פסוק in a way that fits the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the פסוק mentions breasts before the coming of age, which seems to fit רבי מאיר. The answer says the פסוק is not listing which grows first. It is giving a sign: when the breasts are there, you can be sure the hair is already there. That fits the רבנן, who hold the lower sign always comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: It is known for certain
Your breasts (the upper sign)
Your youth; here, the signs of coming of age (the hair)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Once your breasts have come,
it is known that your signs of youth have come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 using the same reading as step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק as a sign, not as an order of growth
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק lists breasts first, so the upper sign grows first, like רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means that once the breasts are there, the hair is surely there already, which fits the רבנן.

steps.title: A second answer: the whole verse speaks only about breasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer. The word 'שדי' in the פסוק means breasts, so the whole פסוק is about breasts and says nothing about hair or about order. The גמרא then begins to explain what הקדוש ברוך הוא was telling ישראל, and that explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: what does 'שדי' mean? The whole פסוק is written about breasts. And this is what הקדוש ברוך הוא was saying to ישראל:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to answer the קשיא. At the end it sets up an explanation of the פסוק's message, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer accepted that the פסוק mentions both breasts and the coming of age. This answer reads 'שדי' as breasts, so the פסוק never mentions the hair at all. If the hair is not mentioned, the פסוק cannot prove anything about which sign comes first.
